question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=x+6$ and $g(x)={x}^{2}.$

First, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ x+6 & ={x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}-x-6 & =0 \\ (x-3)(x+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the limits of integration are from $x=-2$ to $x=3.$

Let's draw our vertical arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/dd8dc332f56d3b851647e5ed0fa8208eb5d3daf6e704a42ab5cffdb78ed78585.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $y=g(x)={x}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $y=f(x)=x+6.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{3}((x+6)^{2}-({x}^{2})^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{3}({x}^{2}+12x+36-{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+6{x}^{2}+36x-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5})\,{|}_{-2}^{3} \\  & =\pi [(\frac{27}{3}+54+108-\frac{243}{5})-(-\frac{8}{3}+24-72+\frac{32}{5})] \\  & =\frac{500\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
